items.title: Gate timing, scope, severity, and preflight precedence are defined
items.statement: The gate runs at configured tier boundaries, defaults to phase-only, supports changed-files, open, or project scope, and prevents advisory iteration-local preflight from replacing the configured boundary gate.

dimension_assessments.summary: Gate execution behavior is substantially defined, but optional editor behaviors and config-change timing remain underspecified.
The advanced capability catalog is explicit, but the supported subset and activation contracts are discretionary.
Config inputs, failed-result flags, summaries, and snapshots are named, but skip/timeout outputs and evidence reference shapes are incomplete.
Core gate contracts are explicit, but enum spelling and evidence storage contracts are inconsistent or ambiguous.
Fail transitions into standard orchestrator policy are defined; timeout, unavailable, skip, and live config-update transitions are not.
LSP-specific protocol and client authority is assigned to Plans/LSPSupport.md while referenced SSOT boundaries are retained.
Document ownership is explicit, but operational ownership of verifier, config propagation, notification, and evidence lifecycle is not allocated.
The standard orchestrator flow, Dashboard/Gate report, user inspection path, and evidence surfaces are identifiable consumers.
Controls and failure-report surfaces are explicit, but GUI validation, persistence, unavailable-state, and toast lifecycle remain open.
Failed diagnostics use standard retry, escalation, or stop policy; timeout and unavailable classification and observability are incomplete.
Mandatory diagnostics snapshots lack redaction, access, encryption, retention, and deletion rules.
Shared config and downstream gate evidence are named, but dependency edges and effective-config propagation rules are absent.
Timeout and evidence locations are named, but skip observability, evidence retention, retrieval, quotas, and cleanup are not operationally defined.
A timeout exists, but whole-project collection and mandatory snapshots have no count, byte, truncation, pagination, caching, or storage bounds.
No compatibility-only notes establish handling for prior config keys, enum spellings, blobs, or evidence formats.
Only plan migration and index validators are declared; runtime and GUI behavioral oracles are absent.
Consequential discretion remains over optional feature scope, enum normalization, GUI lifecycle, evidence storage and privacy, timeout handling, scaling, dependencies, and config propagation.
Key ambiguities include optional feature selection, severity enum identity, evidence destination, timeout classification, compatibility, and effective-config timing.
